title: Grammar
statusNote: Structure is final; the question set is a development set. PRD Section 23.1 item 3 leaves the final questions and difficulty distribution to the team, so this file must be replaced with approved content before the pilot, not treated as approved.
instructions: Choose the option that best completes each sentence.

questions.prompt: She ___ to the library every Saturday.
questions.explanation: A third-person singular subject ('she') takes the -s form of the verb in the present simple: 'she goes'. The other options either ignore the subject ('go') or are not finite verb forms ('going', 'gone').

questions.prompt: I saw ___ elephant at the zoo yesterday.
questions.explanation: 'Elephant' begins with a vowel sound, so the indefinite article is 'an'. 'A' is used before consonant sounds, and 'the' would suggest a specific elephant already known to the listener.
'At' is used with clock times ('at nine o'clock'). 'In' is used with longer periods (months, years), and 'on' with days and dates.

'Since' marks a point in the past that continues to the present, which requires the present perfect: 'I have lived'. The present simple and present continuous describe states that are not anchored this way, and the past simple would imply the situation has ended.

questions.prompt: This exam was ___ than the last one.
questions.explanation: Short one-syllable adjectives form the comparative with -er: 'harder than'. 'Hardest' is the superlative, and 'more hard' is not used because 'hard' takes the -er ending instead.

questions.prompt: The student ___ won the prize is my cousin.
questions.explanation: The relative pronoun refers to a person ('the student') and is the subject of the clause, so 'who' is correct. 'Which' is for things, 'whose' marks possession, and 'what' cannot introduce a defining relative clause.

questions.prompt: If she ___ the earlier train, she would have arrived on time.
questions.explanation: The third conditional describes an unreal past situation: 'if' + past perfect, then 'would have' + past participle. 'Would take' cannot appear in the 'if' clause here, and the present perfect does not fit a hypothetical past.
When a negative adverbial such as 'rarely' opens the sentence, the subject and auxiliary invert: 'have I heard'. Without inversion the sentence is ungrammatical in this position.

questions.prompt: The committee recommended that the report ___ submitted by Friday.
questions.explanation: After verbs of demand and recommendation, formal English uses the base form of the verb in the 'that' clause: 'recommended that the report be submitted'. The indicative forms are not used in this construction in formal writing.
